strategy.angle: The shift from raw compute to operational efficiency as the primary bottleneck for industrial AI scaling.
strategy.audience: Houston-based C-suite executives and operational leads.

draft.hook: The AI gold rush is over; the era of the 'AI tax' has officially begun.
draft.body: NVIDIA’s recent pivot toward 'tokens per watt' efficiency signals a cold reality for Houston’s enterprises: compute power is no longer the scarcest resource—energy efficiency is. While most companies focus on model accuracy, the real competitive advantage for Houston’s energy and industrial sectors lies in optimizing infrastructure for sustainable throughput. If your AI costs scale linearly with your output, you are already behind. At Amplify Intelligence, Leon Coe and I have observed that firms failing to account for the energy-to-compute ratio face a 40% higher operational cost over the next 24 months. How do you bridge this gap? You stop buying generic AI capacity and start building architecturally specific 'AI factories' that align with your specific energy availability. This is the difference between an AI pilot that burns your budget and an industrial-grade engine that drives margin expansion.
draft.closing: Infrastructure is the new strategy. If you aren't calculating your cost-per-token in the same breath as your revenue-per-customer, you're merely subsidizing the hardware giants.
draft.cta: DM me 'EFFICIENCY' if you want to stress-test your current AI architecture against these shifting energy benchmarks.
